subject: Post-call: EvergreenFin - deployment constraints, SLOs & next technical asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom O'Connor <tom.oconnor@evergreenfin.com>, Priya Menon <priya@evergreenfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: EvergreenFin - deployment constraints, SLOs & next technical asks

Tom / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the immediate asks so we can scope a pilot / POC: 

Key pain points you shared
- Inconsistent latency during peak batch scoring windows (spikes to >600ms for 512-token responses).
- High per-token cost for nightly bulk reranking jobs (cost sensitivity for non-real-time workloads).
- Strict data residency and audit requirements for transaction logs and request metadata.

Goals you want to achieve in a 3-month pilot
- 95th percentile tail latency <= 250ms for interactive scoring (single-turn, 256 token internal average).
- Batch throughput of ~25 concurrent long-context reranking jobs with predictable cost targets.
- Audit logs retained for 90 days in your EU region (compliant with internal regs).

Technical constraints / notes we captured
- Current models: a fine-tuned Llama variant (13B) for scoring + a smaller 7B for fast routing/heuristics.
- On-prem gateway with VPC peering required for private deployment; no public egress of raw requests.
- Peak concurrency expected between 13:00-16:00 PT.

Immediate next steps (owners and timing)
1) Evergreen: confirm the infra contact who will share network/VPN constraints and firewall rules (Ethan). Target: Mon 11/8 - TOM
2) Redwood (Marissa): send SLO/throughput template and a short checklist for model compatibility (attached). Target: Fri 11/6 - DONE (attached)
3) Redwood (Ben + Priyom): propose two topology options (private dedicated pool vs hybrid hosted + private routing) and cost delta by 11/9
4) Evergreen: share a small sample reranking workload (anonymized) and a representative prompt set so we can run perf profiles 

Attachments: evergreen-slo-template.xlsx (SLO/traffic breakdown), high-level pricing estimate stub will follow once we pick topology.

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise, I’ll coordinate Ben/Priyom to get the topology options over early next week.

—

Tom / Priya — following up with the topology options we discussed in the call. Attaching a short sketch and the options matrix. High level: 

Option A — Private Dedicated Pool (recommended for tight SLOs)
- Dedicated GPUs in customer VPC via Redwood Private control plane
- No public egress of request payloads; logs routed to your KMS-backed S3
- Expected p95 latency (256 tokens): ~170–220ms depending on instance size; p99 estimate attached
- Cost: higher fixed monthly commit, lower marginal per-token cost for heavy throughput

Option B — Hybrid Hosted + Private Routing
- Live model serving in Redwood Hosted for baseline traffic; burst/critical flows routed to Private nodes in your VPC
- Faster to start; predictable tail by routing long contexts to private pool
- Cost: lower start-up; increased per-token cost on hosted tier during bursts

Attachments: redwood-topology-sketch.png (architecture sketch), evergreen-slo-template.xlsx (SLO template).

Next technical asks from Redwood
- Priyom: can you validate if model weights are the canonical Llama 13B fork + finetune or if there are custom ops that would require build-time adjustments?
- Tom: confirm typical input length distribution (we saw 32–1024 in the call; please narrow if possible).

I’ll follow up with a short p99 estimate (numbers and assumptions) by COB Monday.

—

Tom — quick technical note from our runtime team after I walked through your profile this morning: 

Preliminary performance assumptions (to validate with your sample workload)
- Model: Llama-13B-finetuned variant — we assume standard attention kernels, no custom CUDA ops. If you have custom operators (quantization-specific or fused ops), share a build artifact.
- Latency expectations (single-request, cold vs warm)
  - Warm (KV-cache hit, batch size 1): p95 ~180ms, p99 ~340ms for ~256 tokens on an A100-class private instance with continuous batching disabled for interactive traffic.
  - Cold start or reloaded KV: additional ~120–200ms overhead depending on shard locality.
- Throughput: for batch reranking flows we recommend a dedicated pool with 4–8 GPUs depending on how often the model is used in batch windows. The sample you provide will let us size this precisely.

Network/Deploy notes
- For the hybrid option we will need an allowlist of egress CIDRs: 34.212.0.0/16 and 52.14.128.0/18 (example ranges) — we can exchange final lists once region and AZ placement are confirmed.
- Audit logs: Redwood can stream redacted request metadata to your S3 (KMS envelope encryption). We’ll need a service account and bucket policy to write logs.

Can you confirm:
- Whether the 90-day log retention is acceptable vs your longer-term cold archive?
- Whether the Llama-13B variant uses any tokenizers outside of HuggingFace tokenizers (e.g., custom BPE changes)?

I’ll attach a short checklist and a low-level perf profile matrix after we ingest your sample.

Thanks — Priyom
